rules.statement: Preserve each ratified cube master as authored, including dark-face assignment, symbol, material response and local color modulation.
rules.observable: Orange/right/>_; blue/left/>$; green/top/>#; accepted master appearance remains unchanged.
rules.test: Verify the packaged PNG masters against their ratified SHA-256 hashes and inspect the site/reference usage.

rules.statement: Use Syster as the universal organizational logo or infer behavior from mascot artwork.
rules.observable: Syster is labeled as mascot/reference only.
rules.test: Review identity usage in each fixture.

rules.statement: Regenerate, perspective-transform, re-typeset or geometrically normalize a ratified identity master as an implementation shortcut.
rules.observable: Consumers use packaged masters or exact-fidelity containers; transformations are limited to uniform presentation scaling/cropping that does not redraw the artwork.
rules.test: Compare source hashes and inspect identity implementation for generated text or replacement geometry.

rules.statement: Composite a ratified alpha identity master over a chromatic substrate. Alpha masters are sanctioned on neutral substrates only.
rules.observable: An alpha master appears only on a token from the neutral ramp. Over Signal Orange, Royal Blue or Beret Green the opaque ratified master is used instead.
rules.test: Inspect each identity placement and record its substrate; the cube's dark faces must remain distinguishable from the surface behind them.

rules.statement: Use Space Grotesk as the primary family for interface and authored reference text; do not apply this rule to glyphs already baked into ratified identity artwork.
rules.observable: Live interface/reference text resolves to Space Grotesk; cube symbols remain image content.
rules.test: Inspect computed interface family and verify identity assets are referenced as images rather than reconstructed live text.

rules.statement: Express technical or evidence text with the technical family — IBM Plex Mono — and, where the field says so, with Space Grotesk using weight, tracking and tabular numerals.
rules.observable: Paths, IDs, measurements and evidence labels resolve to the technical family; numeric metadata may use tabular figures.
rules.test: Search profile/reference styles for undeclared font-family overrides and inspect technical specimens.

rules.statement: Read exact approved colors from core/TOKENS.json and generate platform projections from it.
rules.observable: CSS and Kotlin declarations match the token source.
rules.test: Run tools/project_tokens.py --check.

rules.statement: Put white essential normal text on Signal Orange.
rules.observable: Essential text uses an approved legible pairing such as Anthracite on Signal Orange.
rules.test: Inspect contrast of actual text/substrate pairs.

rules.statement: Declare quantity, range, neutral point if applicable, endpoints, missing state and legend for a scalar field.
rules.observable: The field can be interpreted without treating a gradient as ornament.
rules.test: Inspect field annotation and accessible description.

rules.statement: Project an intended mutation as observed success before observation or reconciliation.
rules.observable: Pending text persists until an observation reports the result.
rules.test: Trigger the state fixture and inspect each transition.

rules.statement: Introduce a rounded status, metadata, category, filter, choice or count capsule under any name.
rules.observable: State uses text with optional pip; selection uses a structural treatment; proper controls retain their function.
rules.test: Inspect active control/reference surfaces.

rules.statement: Keep geometry, material, chrome, depth, content, input geometry and allocation independently representable where applicable.
rules.observable: Material and shape may vary without changing semantic role.
rules.test: Compare surface fixture variants and target mappings.

rules.statement: Provide a non-color state cue, an accessible name and visible focus for applicable interactive content.
rules.observable: Keyboard or accessibility service can identify role, state and focus.
rules.test: Keyboard and screen-reader inspection for each profile.

rules.statement: Honor reduced motion and keep asynchronous transitions interruptible.
rules.observable: Reduced-motion mode preserves meaning without continuous decorative animation.
rules.test: Inspect motion preference in available renderers.

rules.statement: Draw interface glyphs from the ratified Tabler subset in assets/icons/. Do not hand-author an SVG glyph, borrow a glyph from another set, or substitute a text character for an icon.
rules.observable: Every interface glyph in a consumer surface resolves to a file listed in assets/icons/icon-manifest.json, at the upstream digest recorded there. Country and organisation flags resolve to the ratified Tabler Flags subset.
rules.test: Run tools/vendor_icons.py --check and confirm no consumer surface contains a hand-authored <svg> glyph or a Unicode character standing in for an icon.

rules.statement: A published token name is the layer id, kebab-cased, under the --gnosix- prefix. No projection may rename a layer id, and no consumer may write a name the system does not publish.
rules.observable: The set of --gnosix-* names in the published web projection equals the set derived from the layer ids in core/TOKENS.json and core/SURFACES.json by the one published function.
rules.test: The naming gate derives the expected name set from the contract and compares it with the published projection. The rule was moved out of the projection and into the contract because a vendored copy of the namespace drifted in spelling while every projection still agreed with itself.

rules.statement: A product may carry its own content palette for what it is showing — a diagram, a chart, a data visualisation, a category of thing — provided it is declared and provided it does not carry the interface. The interface is the system's; the content is the product's.
rules.observable: The colours a product declares as content are named in one place with a reason, and every colour in the interface is one of the system's.
rules.test: The consumer check reports the colours a consumer carries that the system does not have, and a consumer that has declared a content palette is absorbed when what is left is nothing.

rules.statement: A scheme that changes the ink changes the ground the ink is written on. The system's grounds are not dark enough to carry every ink, so a scheme carries the grounds its own ink needs.
rules.observable: Run python3 tools/audit_scheme.py against the scheme: every pairing the system states must still read, on both substrates.
rules.test: The contract's own two schemes pass the audit, and a consumer's scheme passes it before the scheme is applied.

rules.statement: Compose first, paint once. A surface is composed into one canonical boundary before it is filled or stroked: semantic regions compose into a single material boundary, and the surface is painted by one path and one owner.
rules.observable: No independently stroked shell region, no duplicate shell stroke and no profile-private deformation survives a settled surface.
rules.test: Compose the regions of a surface and compare the resulting boundary with the one that is painted: they are the same.

rules.statement: The curvature of a shell is one authority for the whole composition. A region does not carry a radius of its own, and a window's rounding is the shell's rounding.
rules.observable: A window's corner radius equals the shell's radius, and the exposed lower turns consume the same global curvature.
rules.test: Read the radius of the shell and of every window on the output; they are one number.

rules.statement: A settled surface is a canonical state rebuilt from the composition, not the residue of an animation. A transition has no independently renderable primitive, and a rebuild at rest equals a fresh build.
rules.observable: The settled pose is byte-for-byte the pose a fresh build produces, and the transition contributes no layer of its own.
rules.test: Settle a surface, rebuild it from the canonical state, and compare the two renders.

rules.statement: A surface's occupancy is stated, never inferred from its dimensions, and each output resolves its own policy. A compositor's fullscreen is an explicit occupancy class.
rules.observable: The occupancy class is present in the state that the compositor receives; no policy is chosen from a width or a height.
rules.test: Compare the occupancy and the policy of two outputs of the same session; they are resolved independently.

rules.statement: A configuration epoch isolates what a profile may not bleed into another. Private motion state does not cross an epoch.
rules.observable: Applying a configuration to one output does not change the state of another, and a profile's private state does not survive its epoch.
rules.test: Apply a configuration on one output and read the other; it is unchanged.
